subject: Clarify: where Novamed customer requests are processed and subprocessor routing
messages:
From: Hannah Grant <hannah.grant@novamed.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Novamed Security <sec@novamed.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Residency questions — where do requests actually run?

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking time to speak earlier. A few follow-ups from our security team: can you clarify exactly where Novamed customer requests are executed (regions, cloud providers), which subprocessors see payloads, and whether any cross-border transfers can occur for EU customer traffic? We need to understand if we can guarantee "no US processing" for strictly EU data, or whether there are fallback paths that could route through non-EU infra.

Specifically, our security team is asking for:
- A list of regions and cloud providers that may execute inference or store request payloads
- Any CDN/edge or third-party caching subprocessors that might transiently cache data
- Typical retention windows for request payloads, logs, and derived artifacts (embeddings, KV cache)
- How deletion/erasure requests are handled and timelines

Can you point to a single diagram or table that summarizes this so we can attach it to our procurement security packet?

Appreciate a concise, actionable response we can share with our GRC folks.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Grant
Head of IT Security — Novamed

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Grant <hannah.grant@novamed.com>
Cc: Novamed Security <sec@novamed.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Nov 2025 11:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Residency questions — where do requests actually run?

Hannah — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary (high level first, followed by operational detail). I attached a one-page residency diagram and a processing matrix for easy consumption.

High-level summary
- Default routing: inbound requests are routed to the region closest to the customer endpoint (latency-first). For EU customers that means we prefer EU regions (e.g., GCP europe-west3, AWS eu-west-1).
- Subprocessors: the runtime may use compute/storage/infra across major cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure) plus a small set of edge/CDN and telemetry subprocessors (Fastly for CDN, Datadog for metrics). See attached matrix for full roster and minimum legal names and contact points.
- Cross-border transfers: with default hosted routing, we do not guarantee geographic isolation — there are fallback and burst paths that can route to non-EU regions if EU capacity is saturated (we surface these events in Console and via alerts). For contractual guarantees (no US processing for EU traffic) we offer two options: Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools in a selected region) or Private deployment (VPC/on‑prem) which avoid cross-border execution.

Operational detail (what we mean by "processed" and "transient copies")
- Inference execution: model inference occurs on GPU instances in the region selected for the request. For hosted customers, that selection is typically automatic but can be pinned via the Console or API (region pinning).
- Persistent storage: user-provided payloads are stored only as needed:
  - Request logs & traces: default retention 14 days
  - Debug snapshots (when enabled by customer): retained for 30 days unless otherwise requested
  - Derived artifacts (embeddings, cached vectors): default retention 90 days; can be configured per-account
  - KV caches and model working state: ephemeral in-memory caches by default; persistent checkpointing is applied only for long-running sessions and those checkpoints are encrypted and TTL'd per account policy
- Encryption: all data in transit is TLS 1.2+; at-rest encryption uses provider-managed keys by default (AWS/GCP/Azure KMS). Enterprise customers may bring their own keys (BYOK/HSM integration available).

Deletion & erasure
- Self-serve: customers can request data deletion via the Console or API. For hosted accounts we expose a /data/delete endpoint that queues a complete erase from active storage and mark items for GC.
- Timeline: typical complete deletion (remove from active storage + indices) completes within 72 hours; longer-lived artifacts (backups, analytic aggregates) are purged within 30 days unless an exception exists for legal holds.
- Verification: for enterprise contracts we provide a deletion certificate and audit log showing timestamps and the records removed.

Cross-border specifics and controls
- Region pinning: if you pin to an EU region we route inference only to pinned regions unless an explicit failover is triggered (we document failovers in an incident/alert).
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to non-EU capacity can occur for burst/bottleneck conditions. That behavior can be disabled for Dedicated/Private plans.
- SCCs & transfer mechanisms: Redwood supports SCCs and other lawful transfer mechanisms for EU->non-EU transfers; we can include SCCs in the DPA and provide subprocessors list on request.

Next steps
- I attached the residency diagram and a matrix that lists subprocessors, region tags, and the type of processing they perform. If you need contract-level commitments (e.g., strict EU execution with no fallbacks), I recommend we loop in Marissa from our contracts team so we can scope Dedicated or Private options.

Attachments: residency-diagram.png, data-processing-matrix.xlsx

Best,

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0189

From: Hannah Grant <hannah.grant@novamed.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 08:45:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Residency questions — where do requests actually run?

Thanks, that helps a lot. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- For "derived artifacts": embeddings are considered PHI in some of our workflows. Can embeddings be configured to be deleted immediately (zero-retention) after generation?
- Encryption: can you confirm that keys used for at-rest encryption never leave the customer's selected region when BYOK is used? Our lawyers are particularly worried about key escrow or key material replication to non-EU KMS.
- Finally — if we pin to an EU region, are there any background processes (indexing, enrichment, telemetry) that still talk to US-based subprocessors and could cause EU data to transit US networks?

Appreciate the precision here — our legal team will want explicit language.

Hannah

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Grant <hannah.grant@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Novamed Security <sec@novamed.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 09:30:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Residency questions — where do requests actually run?

Hannah — quick answers inline, and looping in Marissa to cover contractual guarantees and DPA/SCC language.

- Embeddings retention: yes — embeddings retention is configurable. For hosted accounts we can set embeddings retention to 0 days (generation-only, then immediate deletion) as a runtime setting. For strict zero-retention we recommend a short test to validate behavior and then we can add an appendix to the DPA.

- BYOK and key locality: when you use BYOK, key material remains under your control and we do not export key material out of the region. We integrate with customer KMS endpoints and support Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS, and Google Cloud KMS. For customers who need additional assurance, we support HSM-backed keys and can include a clause preventing cross-region key replication.

- Background processes & telemetry: some non-essential services (global telemetry aggregation, SRE analytics) may be routed to non-EU endpoints by default. However for customers that require strict in-region processing we offer a "data residency hardening" option which disables forwarding of telemetry/aggregates and routes required services through EU-only endpoints. This is commonly paired with Dedicated or Private deployments.

Marissa — can we prepare a DPA appendix and SCC wording for Novamed that covers: EU-only execution pin, BYOK key locality guarantee clause, and an embeddings-zero-retention option? Also include the up-to-date subprocessors roster and a signed deletion attestation. I have attached the residency matrix; happy to walk through details in a short call.

If helpful, I can schedule a 30-min call with our Contracts + Security folks tomorrow.

Thanks,
Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
